summary: Unexpected model anchoring lapse during weighted slice rebalance causing mixed-variant responses
description:
Summary: NovaLexa reported intermittent mixed-model outputs for a small percentage of requests immediately after a weighted slice rebalance of their dedicated pool. Tenant had explicitly requested a model version pin to redwood-13b-instruct-v1, but 3–5% of their requests were routed to an alternate variant for ~18 minutes. Impact was visible in production logs and user-reported quality regressions.

Observed behavior: tenant traffic was mostly routed correctly to pinned model, but a minority of sessions received responses from the new canary variant (open-llama-13b-q4). Those responses differed in tokenization/formatting and triggered downstream validation failures in NovaLexa's ingestion pipeline.
impact: Customer-facing: degraded output consistency for NovaLexa Analytics (dedicated). Approximately 3-5% of calls in us-west produced responses from an unpinned variant for ~18 minutes; several downstream ingestion failures and automated alerts were triggered. No data exfiltration suspected. SLA risk: near miss for monthly availability for this tenant.
timeline: 2026-03-10T10:02:00Z - NovaLexa support ticket opened, reports inconsistent outputs (attached sample responses).
2026-03-10T10:12:00Z - Support triage: reproduced small fraction of mixed responses in us-west; escalated to SRE.
2026-03-10T10:28:00Z - SRE noticed orchestrator slice rebalance job completed at 10:15Z; edge propagation logs show partial routing metadata mismatch.
2026-03-10T10:45:00Z - Manual mitigation applied: tenant forcibly bound to stable variant at edge layer; customer verified improvement.
2026-03-10T11:00:00Z - Traffic stabilised; follow-up investigation continued into commit/lease handoff and cache propagation timing.

2026-03-12T09:30:00Z - Root-cause hypothesis draft: rebalance logic allowed active leases to be transiently reclassified across orchestrator epochs before edge cache TTL expired, causing ~18m window of mixed routing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a dedicated pool with a pinned model version for a tenant and a concurrent weighted canary slice assigned to same pool.
2) Trigger a slice rebalance (e.g., change weights or scale down a slice) during normal traffic in prod (us-west).
3) Monitor tenant request routing at the edge and serving-runtime for 30 minutes post-rebalance; inspect session tokens/affinity headers.
4) Verify whether any active sessions are routed to the alternate variant while pin appears set in control plane.
logs: edge-proxy[10:16:07Z] INFO route-eval tenant=novalexa session=abc123 bound_variant=redwood-13b-instruct-v1 decision=serve (cache_ttl=300s)
orchestrator[10:15:22Z] INFO rebalance completed slice_id=slice-7 epoch=203 commit_id=sha256:7b9f...
edge-proxy[10:21:11Z] WARN route-eval tenant=novalexa session=abc123 bound_variant=redwood-13b-instruct-v1 decision=fallback serve_variant=open-llama-13b-q4 reason=variant_unavailable
serving-runtime[10:20:59Z] ERROR kvcache-miss tenant=novalexa key=session-affinity-abc123 status=miss
ingestion-pipeline[10:22:04Z] ERROR validation_failed tenant=novalexa request_id=req-998 sample_mismatch=expected:redwood got:open-llama
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Edge cache TTL and orchestrator epoch commit were out of sync, allowing stale affinity decisions during a short window.
Hypothesis B: Lease handoff logic in orchestrator allowed transient reclassification of active sessions when slices were merged, but did not emit a bounded rebind event to the edge layer.

Findings: Edge logs show explicit fallback decisions (serve_variant=open-llama-13b-q4) while control plane still reported tenant pinned to redwood-13b-instruct-v1. Serving runtime reported KV cache misses for several session keys coincident with rebalance epoch. No evidence of auth or header mutation.
Reproducibility: Non-deterministic; reproduces reliably when rebalance timing coincides with active long-lived sessions that hold affinity leases older than edge cache TTL.
workaround: Applied: forced tenant-level override at edge (session rebind) to stable variant and cleared route cache for affected edge nodes; instructed customer to retry failing ingestion items. This restored consistent routing within ~3 minutes for new requests.
resolution_notes: Mitigation in place (edge override). Short-term patch proposed: emit explicit rebind events from orchestrator when slice topology changes and proactively invalidate edge affinity for affected tenants. Long-term: adjust rebalance algorithm to coordinate lease handoff and edge cache invalidation. Engineering owners: Luis Chen (serving), Priya Rao (orchestrator). Postmortem and CL scheduled.

Luis Chen (SRE) 2026-03-10T10:20Z: Observed fallback logs despite pin. Kicked off edge cache clear and temporary override. Need orchestration trace.
Priya Rao (Orchestrator) 2026-03-11T08:40Z: Noted that rebalance commit does not currently publish a tenant-level rebind event. Drafting small change to emit event on slice merge.
Customer (NovaLexa) 2026-03-10T11:10Z: Confirmed that after override their ingestion resumed successfully. Would like timeline and permanent fix.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to land rebind-event patch to orchestrator and add automated edge cache invalidation hook (owner: Priya Rao).
2) Run a controlled repro in staging with long-lived sessions and rebalance to validate fix (owner: Luis Chen).
3) Schedule postmortem with CS, SRE, and Orchestrator team; notify customer timeline and planned fix window.
4) Add monitoring alert for 'small-fraction mixed-variant rate' per tenant during rebalances to catch regressions early.
